title: Coarse filtration by integral ideals and smaller-support factors
statement: Let $X$ be a Noetherian scheme [def-pc-scheme, pqf-def-locnoeth, def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions] and $F$ a finitely presented $\mathcal O_X$-module [def-weil-pbc-module-finite-type-presentation, def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Its support is $\{x\mid F_x\ne0\}$ [def-weil-pbc-module-stalk]. There is a finite increasing subobject chain $0=c_0\leq\cdots\leq c_m=F$ such that each consecutive quotient $Q_j=\operatorname{Coker}(c_j\to c_{j+1})$ satisfies one of two alternatives: (a) there are an integral scheme $Z$ [def-pc-integral-scheme], a closed immersion $i:Z\to X$ [def-weil-closed-immersion], and a quasi-coherent ideal $I\subseteq\mathcal O_Z$ represented by IdealSheafData, with $Q_j\cong i_*I$ [def-pc-module-pullback]; or (b) $Q_j$ is finitely presented and $\overline{\operatorname{Supp}(Q_j)}\subsetneq\overline{\operatorname{Supp}(F)}$. A subobject is an isomorphism class of monomorphisms, and consecutive quotients use the induced inclusions of representatives. The chain need not be strict and length zero is allowed. No filtration is asserted for the factors in alternative (b).

proof.text: Convert finite presentation to coherence using the Noetherian coherence equivalence. A coherent module has closed support. Prove the stronger integral-ideal filtration assertion locally by well-founded induction on closed support; this proof does not import the stronger theorem module.

For empty support, use the public sheaf stalk-detection theorem and faithfulness of the module-to-sheaf forgetful functor to prove that the module is zero. On any scheme, subobjects of a zero module are subsingleton, so the constant bottom chain of length zero has bottom and top endpoints. Transport coherence from the zero object to the bottom subobject using the public coherent-kernel-cokernel-sum theorem. This needs neither local Noetherianity nor coherence of the ambient module.

For reducible support, the closed-union characterization of preirreducibility gives two proper closed subsets covering the support. The support-union exact sequence gives coherent submodule and cokernel with support contained in those subsets. Apply the strict-support induction hypothesis to both and concatenate their filtrations using the extension lemma.

For nonempty irreducible support, sobriety supplies a generic point. Apply the irreducible-support step with the strict-support induction hypothesis. Its J-adic and generic-inclusion argument constructs the filtration without importing cyclic argument-step modules.

Apply the local induction assertion to F and its closed support. Retain the same chain and endpoints, forget coherence of its subobjects and the nonzero/coherence conditions on its ideals, and inject every integral-ideal quotient into the first disjunct. No assertion about the smaller-support disjunct is required.

proof_origin.place: Tag 01YF support induction: empty, reducible, and irreducible cases; the irreducible step explicitly takes the smaller-support induction hypothesis. Cyclic J-adic and generic-step imports are kept only as the split node proof plan.

lean.statement:
theorem exists_finitePresentation_support_reduction_filtration
    (X : Scheme.{u}) [IsNoetherian X] (F : X.Modules) [F.IsFinitePresentation] :
    ∃ (m : ℕ) (c : Fin (m + 1) → Subobject F) (hc : Monotone c),
      c 0 = ⊥ ∧ c (Fin.last m) = ⊤ ∧
      ∀ j : Fin m,
        let Q := cokernel (Subobject.ofLE (c j.castSucc) (c j.succ)
          (hc j.castSucc_le_succ))
        (∃ (Z : Scheme.{u}) (i : Z ⟶ X),
          IsClosedImmersion i ∧ IsIntegral Z ∧
          ∃ I : Z.IdealSheafData, Nonempty (Q ≅ (pushforward i).obj I.toModules)) ∨
        (Q.IsFinitePresentation ∧
          closure {x : X | ¬ Subsingleton (Q.presheaf.stalk x)} ⊂
            closure {x : X | ¬ Subsingleton (F.presheaf.stalk x)})
